references.text: Moses also built an altar and called it 'The Lord is my banner' (JHVH Nissi), showing the same pattern of giving an altar a name that describes God's character.
God's command to build altars of earth or stone, which Gideon followed when he built an altar for the Lord.
Jacob built an altar and called it El-Elohe-Israel, showing the same tradition of naming altars to honor God.
Jacob built an altar in Bethel and called the place El-Betel, a parallel to Gideon's naming of the altar.
The Messiah is called 'Prince of Peace' (Sar Shalom), linking to the altar Gideon named 'The Lord is peace' (JHVH Shalom).
God promises a 'covenant of peace' with His people, showing that peace (shalom) is a central aspect of God's relationship with Israel.
Christ is our peace (eirene), fulfilling the meaning of the altar JHVH Shalom – The Lord is peace.
God's peace that surpasses all understanding guards hearts and minds – a deeper fulfillment of 'The Lord is peace'.
